**Digne Cathedral** (French: _Cathédrale Saint-Jérome de Digne_) is a Latin Catholicchurch located in the town of Digne-les-Bains, France. The cathedral has been a _monument historique_ since 1906.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne_Cathedral#cite_note-1) It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and Sisteron, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Digne Cathedral, west front
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town's population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, **Notre-Dame-du-Bourg** (_Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne_), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.

**Digne-les-Bains**, or simply and historically Digne, is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department in the **Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur** region of Southeastern **France** on the **Bléone river**.
**Tourism and main attractions**
Digne Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church. The cathedral has been a monument historique since 1906. It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and **Sisteron**, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town’s population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, Notre-Dame-du-Bourg (Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.
The Saint-Jérôme de Digne Cathedral is the second cathedral in the city. Located in the heart of the city, on the Rochas hill, from the 16th century it replaced the original episcopal seat located at Notre-Dame-du-Bourg.
Antoine de Guiramand, bishop of Digne, from 1479, was behind the construction of Saint-Jérôme cathedral. The building, erected from 1490 to 1500, is the work of Antoine Brollion, master mason in Barcelonnette. Originally, it had a central nave of four bays flanked by side aisles onto which chapels were added during the 17th century.
The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes Church was built in 1870 on the Mountain of the Cross, north of Digne, though at the bottom of the slope. The brick walls are its main feature, with its large size.
The chapel of Saint-Vincent belonged to an abbey or priory. It is still in good condition. The Chapel of the Cross, located nearby, is gradually becoming a ruin.

The remains of fortifications can be recognised if one pays attention to the plan of the old town around the central district, built on the heights. Some of the walls and some towers which surrounded the city from the 14th century can still be seen. These remains of ramparts are currently based in the landscape of the dwellings.
The town of Digne was immortalized by Victor Hugo who placed the beginning of his famous novel Les Misérables there.
Museum of the Haute-Provence geological reserve and its butterfly garden.
Gassendi Museum with modern museography allowing the public to move from art to science, from ancient to contemporary through a journey through time. Its archeology section was founded in 1889.
World War II Museum. Documents and period objects evoke the strategic role of Digne-les-Bains in Alpine defense.
Alexandra David-Néel Museum, located in her house.

# **Digne Cathedral****,**Gothic cathedral in Digne-les-Bains, France
Audio guide· About one minute Preparing your audio guide…The audio guide could not be loaded, please retry.Sign in to listen to the audio guide
Digne Cathedral is a Gothic structure marked by pointed arches, ribbed vaulting, and detailed stonework characteristic of southeastern French architecture. The interior rises with slender columns that support a network of stone ribs dividing the space into side chapels and a central nave.
Bishop Antoine de Guiramand ordered the cathedral built from 1490 to 1500 to replace Notre-Dame-du-Bourg, as the town moved to the defensible hill of Rochas. The master mason was Antoine Brollion of Barcelonnette. From 1846 to 1862 diocesan architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly added a bay and a facade modelled on 13th-century Gothic; in 1853 Pierre Boulanger forged the door ironwork. It was listed in 1906 and became a co-cathedral on 31 July 1962.
The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Jerome, and since 31 July 1962 it has served as co-cathedral of the Diocese of Digne, Riez and Sisteron alongside Notre-Dame-du-Bourg. Its 1865 Cavaillé-Coll tribune organ, set in a neo-Gothic case against the facade, has 21 stops on two manuals and a pedalboard and has been classified for its instrumental part since 20 October 1976; the bell dates from 1618.
The cathedral is easily reached on foot from the town center and sits at a central location in Digne. Morning or late afternoon visits work best, when light enters through the windows and illuminates the stonework throughout the interior.
The tribune organ was built by Cavaillé-Coll in 1865 and placed against the inner face of the facade in a neo-Gothic case; its instrumental part has been classified since 20 October 1976. It has 21 stops on two manuals and a pedalboard. The bell dates from 1618.

The building, erected from 1490 to 1500, is the work of Antoine Brollion, master mason in Barcelonnette. Originally, it had a central nave of four bays flanked by side aisles onto which chapels were added during the 17th century.
The Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes Church was built in 1870 on the Mountain of the Cross, north of Digne, though at the bottom of the slope. The brick walls are its main feature, with its large size.
The chapel of Saint-Vincent belonged to an abbey or priory. It is still in good condition. The Chapel of the Cross, located nearby, is gradually becoming a ruin.

Audio guide· About one minute Preparing your audio guide…The audio guide could not be loaded, please retry.Sign in to listen to the audio guide
Digne Cathedral is a Gothic structure marked by pointed arches, ribbed vaulting, and detailed stonework characteristic of southeastern French architecture. The interior rises with slender columns that support a network of stone ribs dividing the space into side chapels and a central nave.
Bishop Antoine de Guiramand ordered the cathedral built from 1490 to 1500 to replace Notre-Dame-du-Bourg, as the town moved to the defensible hill of Rochas. The master mason was Antoine Brollion of Barcelonnette. From 1846 to 1862 diocesan architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly added a bay and a facade modelled on 13th-century Gothic; in 1853 Pierre Boulanger forged the door ironwork. It was listed in 1906 and became a co-cathedral on 31 July 1962.
The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Jerome, and since 31 July 1962 it has served as co-cathedral of the Diocese of Digne, Riez and Sisteron alongside Notre-Dame-du-Bourg. Its 1865 Cavaillé-Coll tribune organ, set in a neo-Gothic case against the facade, has 21 stops on two manuals and a pedalboard and has been classified for its instrumental part since 20 October 1976; the bell dates from 1618.
The cathedral is easily reached on foot from the town center and sits at a central location in Digne. Morning or late afternoon visits work best, when light enters through the windows and illuminates the stonework throughout the interior.

**Digne Cathedral** (French: _Cathédrale Saint-Jérome de Digne_) is a Latin Catholicchurch located in the town of Digne-les-Bains, France. The cathedral has been a _monument historique_ since 1906.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne_Cathedral#cite_note-1) It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and Sisteron, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Digne Cathedral, west front
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town's population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, **Notre-Dame-du-Bourg** (_Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne_), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.

# **Digne Cathedral****,**Gothic cathedral in Digne-les-Bains, France
Audio guide· About one minute Preparing your audio guide…The audio guide could not be loaded, please retry.Sign in to listen to the audio guide
Digne Cathedral is a Gothic structure marked by pointed arches, ribbed vaulting, and detailed stonework characteristic of southeastern French architecture. The interior rises with slender columns that support a network of stone ribs dividing the space into side chapels and a central nave.
Bishop Antoine de Guiramand ordered the cathedral built from 1490 to 1500 to replace Notre-Dame-du-Bourg, as the town moved to the defensible hill of Rochas. The master mason was Antoine Brollion of Barcelonnette. From 1846 to 1862 diocesan architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly added a bay and a facade modelled on 13th-century Gothic; in 1853 Pierre Boulanger forged the door ironwork. It was listed in 1906 and became a co-cathedral on 31 July 1962.
The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Jerome, and since 31 July 1962 it has served as co-cathedral of the Diocese of Digne, Riez and Sisteron alongside Notre-Dame-du-Bourg. Its 1865 Cavaillé-Coll tribune organ, set in a neo-Gothic case against the facade, has 21 stops on two manuals and a pedalboard and has been classified for its instrumental part since 20 October 1976; the bell dates from 1618.
The cathedral is easily reached on foot from the town center and sits at a central location in Digne. Morning or late afternoon visits work best, when light enters through the windows and illuminates the stonework throughout the interior.
The tribune organ was built by Cavaillé-Coll in 1865 and placed against the inner face of the facade in a neo-Gothic case; its instrumental part has been classified since 20 October 1976. It has 21 stops on two manuals and a pedalboard. The bell dates from 1618.

The **arrondissement of Digne-les-Bains** is like a special district or area in France. It is part of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azurregion. The main city, or _capital_, of this district is Digne-les-Bains. This city is also the _prefecture_, meaning it's where the main government offices for the whole department are located.

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.

## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
An arrondissement is made up of smaller parts called _cantons_ and _communes_. Think of them like smaller towns and their surrounding areas.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
### Cantons
After some changes in France, cantons are no longer just inside one arrondissement. This means a canton might include small towns (communes) that belong to different arrondissements.
In the Digne-les-Bains arrondissement, there are 6 cantons. Four of these cantons have all their communes completely inside this arrondissement:

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.
texts.3:
## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

An arrondissement is made up of smaller parts called _cantons_ and _communes_. Think of them like smaller towns and their surrounding areas.

After some changes in France, cantons are no longer just inside one arrondissement. This means a canton might include small towns (communes) that belong to different arrondissements.

*   Oraison (partly in this arrondissement)

The **arrondissement of Digne-les-Bains** is like a special district or area in France. It is part of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azurregion. The main city, or _capital_, of this district is Digne-les-Bains. This city is also the _prefecture_, meaning it's where the main government offices for the whole department are located.

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.

## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
An arrondissement is made up of smaller parts called _cantons_ and _communes_. Think of them like smaller towns and their surrounding areas.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
### Cantons
After some changes in France, cantons are no longer just inside one arrondissement. This means a canton might include small towns (communes) that belong to different arrondissements.
In the Digne-les-Bains arrondissement, there are 6 cantons. Four of these cantons have all their communes completely inside this arrondissement:
*   Digne-les-Bains-1  
*   Digne-les-Bains-2  
*   Oraison (partly in this arrondissement)  
*   Riez  
*   Seyne (partly in this arrondissement)  
*   Valensole

The arrondissement of Digne-les-Bains was created in 1800.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissement_of_Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-4) At the January 2017 reorganization of the arrondissements of Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, it lost nine communes to the arrondissement of Castellane and 16 communes to the arrondissement of Forcalquier, and it gained six communes from the arrondissement of Forcalquier.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrondissement_of_Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-arrete-5)
